tips for not sucking at xcom
Which one, EU, EW or 2? Between them there are plenty of gameplay changes that require sometimes considerably different approaches.

Right!

Ahh ... a couple of things I can think of quickly:

Tactical:

  • Use your gadgets. The game offers tons of things to keep enemies from dealing damage to you, like the mimetic beacon or flashbangs. Use them aggressively. Along those lines ..

  • There's no kill like overkill! Use grenadiers, build exosuits and use their rocket launchers. It's often better to "waste" a rocket or grenade to make a guaranteed kill on even a small, non-"boss" type of enemy rather than trying to save it for the perfect opportunity only to have that remaining, single trooper get a critical kill on one of your soldiers.

  • Seize attack opportunities / don't bite off more than you can chew. Similar to the above, when you're in a mission where you start concealed (and especially when you're on a timer), don't try to get that perfect ambush set up that you expect to totally take out 6 enemies at once. If you have a good opportunity to kill a single "pod" of enemies (a group of 3 or 4 of them), go for it! It's often better to definitely take out 2 or 3 enemies than to possibly take out 5 or 6, only to have the remnants of the bigger group aggravated and your soldiers now exposed to them when they're not dead.

Generally, don't try to overextend yourself by advancing too far and activating new pods of enemies unless you're prepared to take them on. Essentially you'll have to aim for being able to kill every enemy you currently see in a single turn, before they get a turn to deal damage on you, so you'll want to minimize the number of "activated" enemies at any given point in time, but of course that's always a balancing act between playing defensively and trying to beat the timer on timed missions.

On non-timed missions, however, like base attack missions, you have essentially full control over the pacing and can use this to your advantage. Be very, very careful about advancing in those missions so as not to activate enemy pods when you're not prepared to face them. When in doubt, rather put all your units on overwatch and end the turn than to move a unit further ahead even by a single tile if that might reveal new enemies. In general, make very liberal use of overwatch in these missions and just play defensively.

Strategic:

  • Focus research on armor and weapons. I'd personally say armor is probably even more important than weapons, but it's a bit of a toss up. If your guys are well armored but can't deal enough damage to take out enemies in a single turn, the enemies will eventually be able to chew through the armor. On the other hand, having good guns won't protect you against inevitable hits that you just have to take every now and then, and those will hurt even worse if they're criticals, so that means no armor = no soldiers at some point. Plus, I'd argue that with the abundance of gadgets and grenades available, there are good ways to compensate for the weaker weapons for a fair bit in favor of researching armor first. So definitely make that your utmost priority.

Finally, if you absolutely cannot enjoy the game at all because it's too difficult, don't be afraid to tweak some things yourself (which is really easy by just editing some .ini files) or use mods to loosen up the difficulty. I've been using a mod that lets me modify the mission timer and increased it by two turns from the vanilla settings and I feel this is much more appropriate. I've had missions where I literally could not reach and protect a target in the original time limit because I got unlucky with where my squad spawned and where the objective / enemies would spawn, whereas in other missions you can often spawn essentially right next to the objective. I think that's rather stupid and I feel like I should at least have a fighting chance, so the increase of 2 turns over the original value makes this possible but still keeps just enough pressure on me that I cannot play super defensively and have a guaranteed win.

I'd just like to add some emphasis to your tip to use flashbangs. They are HUGELY useful. Disorientation is a useful debuff to smack an enemy group with, but they also disrupt sectoid mind control of your troops. Further, if a sectoid has a psi-zombie raised, hitting the sectoid with a flashbang will instantly kill the zombie.

First thing I need to introduce you to is the Standard Anti-ADVENT Advancing DefenseTM or S.A.A.DTM which consists of moving up one leader (usually a ranger or specialist) to scout and then having everyone else follow behind so that any alien pods are activated on the first move of your turn and you can position the squad in better cover and have a full turn of shots.

You may have noticed this is ineffective against Burrowing Chryssalids as they can move and attack immediately upon being triggered.

Well it's time to introduce you to the Standard Anti-Chryssalid PositionTM or S.A.P.TM.

It is IMO one of the few things that Sword spec rangers do better than anyone else. And is primarily used in missions where you know that many of enemies are Chryssalids.

Just like S.A.A.DTM you want a point guard (This time you specifically want a Sword ranger, that has the ability to automatically counter-attack foes in melee range). Unlike with the S.A.A.DTM however you want to move up the rest of your squad first(as carefully as the timer/civilian count allows) and then overwatch your entire squad before moving the ranger forward. Burrowed Chryssalid(s) will then unburrow to attack the ranger eating a face full of hot overwatch plasma shots and be killed. If one manages to survive the overwatch the Ranger should be able to finish it off with their sword.

It is not recommended to use the S.A.A.DTM in missions where higher priority targets than Chryssalids are known to be present (Sectopods, Gatekeepers, and possibly Codex's) as you will likely get more use out of Flashbangs/EMP bombs than overwatch against these foes.
